heading: Cloud TPU generations
text:
Cloud TPU generations
Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) are accelerators for machine learning. This set documents four generations, which share most concepts and tasks but differ in their values.

heading: Cloud TPU generations
text:
Cloud TPU generations
Each generation has an introduction, a specifications topic, a configurations topic and a VM types topic. Values such as chips per pod are stored once as keys, so a corrected value changes every page that shows it.

heading: TPU v5e

TPU v5e

heading: TPU7x (Ironwood)
text:
TPU7x (Ironwood)
TPU7x (Ironwood) is the generation for the largest training and inference workloads. Each chip has 2 TensorCores and 4 SparseCores, and a pod holds up to 9216 chips.

heading: TPU7x (Ironwood)
text:
TPU7x (Ironwood)
Use the specification topic to size a slice, the configurations topic to choose a slice shape, and the VM types topic to see what each VM provides.
Important: The Cloud TPU API is no longer under active development and is not supported on TPU7x (Ironwood) and later. Create TPU7x (Ironwood) capacity with Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) or Compute Engine.
Note: JAX and PyTorch are supported on TPU7x (Ironwood). TensorFlow is not.

heading: TPU7x (Ironwood) memory hierarchy
text:
TPU7x (Ironwood) memory hierarchy
How high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and host memory are organized on a TPU7x (Ironwood) chip.

heading: High-bandwidth memory
text:
TPU7x (Ironwood) memory hierarchy > High-bandwidth memory
Each chip has 192 GiB of HBM, with bandwidth of approximately 7.37 TB/s. The large capacity allows large batch sizes, which can improve throughput. HBM can still be a bottleneck for memory-bound vector operations or inefficient data access patterns.

heading: Dual-chiplet design
text:
TPU7x (Ironwood) memory hierarchy > Dual-chiplet design
Each chip has two chiplets. Each chiplet is a self-contained unit with one TensorCore, two SparseCores and 96 GiB of HBM.

heading: Host memory
text:
TPU7x (Ironwood) memory hierarchy > Host memory
The host's main memory connects to the chip with much lower bandwidth than HBM. You can still use it to offload activations or optimizer states and free HBM, which helps with memory pressure in large models.

heading: Create a TPU VM
text:
Create a TPU VM
Create a TPU VM for one generation. The command and software version depend on the generation, so build this topic with that generation's DITAVAL file.

heading: prereq
text:
Create a TPU VM > prereq
You have a Google Cloud project with the Cloud TPU API enabled and quota in your chosen zone.

heading: Create a TPU VM
text:
Create a TPU VM
Step: Set the project for the gcloud CLI:
```
gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID
```

heading: Create a TPU VM
text:
Create a TPU VM
Step: Create the TPU v5e VM:
```
gcloud compute tpus tpu-vm create TPU_NAME \
  --zone=ZONE \
  --accelerator-type=ACCELERATOR_TYPE \
  --version=v2-alpha-tpuv5-lite
```

heading: Create a TPU VM
text:
Create a TPU VM
Step: Create the TPU v5p VM:
```
gcloud compute tpus tpu-vm create TPU_NAME \
  --zone=ZONE \
  --accelerator-type=ACCELERATOR_TYPE \
  --version=v2-alpha-tpuv5
```

text:
Create a TPU VM
Step: Create TPU7x (Ironwood) capacity with GKE or Compute Engine, using the tpu7x-standard-4t machine type.
Important: The Cloud TPU API is no longer under active development and is not supported on TPU7x (Ironwood) and later. Create TPU7x (Ironwood) capacity with Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) or Compute Engine.

heading: Create a TPU VM
text:
Create a TPU VM
Step (optional): To keep the VM off the public internet, add the --internal-ips flag.
Tip: To create a TPU VM without an external IP address, add the --internal-ips flag. The VM can then reach Google APIs and services only through Private Google Access.

heading: Networking and access for Cloud TPU VMs
text:
Networking and access for Cloud TPU VMs
Choose the network, subnetwork and IP addressing for a TPU VM, and decide how it reaches Google APIs.

heading: Custom network and subnetwork
text:
Networking and access for Cloud TPU VMs > Custom network and subnetwork
By default a TPU VM uses the default network. Specify a custom network and subnetwork when you create the VM to place it in your own VPC.

heading: External and internal IP addresses
text:
Networking and access for Cloud TPU VMs > External and internal IP addresses
A TPU VM gets an external IP address by default. To create one without an external IP address, use the --internal-ips flag with gcloud compute tpus queued-resources create or gcloud compute tpus tpu-vm create. With the REST API, set enable_external_ips to false in the network_config of the request body.

heading: Private Google Access
text:
Networking and access for Cloud TPU VMs > Private Google Access
A TPU VM without an external IP address can reach Google APIs and services through Private Google Access on its subnetwork. SSH access needs either an external IP address or Private Google Access.

heading: Optical transceiver modules (illustrative)
text:
Optical transceiver modules (illustrative)
A pluggable optical transceiver turns the electrical signals on a host board into light for a fiber link, and back. This topic uses an original 3D model of an OSFP-style module to show its parts.

heading: Optical transceiver modules (illustrative)
text:
Optical transceiver modules (illustrative)
OSFP stands for Octal Small Form Factor Pluggable. The OSFP MSA group announced the form factor in March 2017 for 400G optics, with eight electrical lanes, and designed it to carry 800G modules as lane speeds rose.
[Image: Animated 3D model of a pluggable optical transceiver turning on its axis]
Note: The model is an original, generic design for illustration. It is not a Google part or any vendor's product.

heading: Parts of the module
text:
Optical transceiver modules (illustrative) > Parts of the module
Heat-sink fins
Run along the top of the shell and carry heat into the switch's airflow.
Optical port
The front opening where the fiber connector plugs in.
Pull tab
Releases the latch so you can remove the module from its cage.
Edge connector
Gold contacts at the rear that mate with the host connector inside the cage.
